name: Autumn Budget 2025
groups: Getting inflation down and tackling the cost of living
Tackling child poverty and reforming welfare
Cutting waste and investing in public services
Modernising motoring tax and supporting the British automative industry
Previously announced policy and other changes

measures.name: Renewables Obligation: Fund 75% of the domestic share of the Renewables Obligation via the Exchequer over the Spending Review period
measures.group: Getting inflation down and tackling the cost of living
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Warm Homes Plan: Increase funding for the Warm Homes Plan and expand the Warm Home Discount Scheme
measures.group: Getting inflation down and tackling the cost of living
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Fuel Duty: Cancel uprating for 2026-27; extend the 5p cut in rates to 31 August 2026, then increase by 1p from 1 September 2026, 2p from 1 December 2026, and 2p from 1 March 2027
measures.group: Getting inflation down and tackling the cost of living
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Rail Fares: Freeze rail fares in England for one year from 1 March 2026
measures.group: Getting inflation down and tackling the cost of living
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Health and Social Care: Freeze NHS prescription charges in England for one year from 1 April 2026
measures.group: Getting inflation down and tackling the cost of living
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Universal Credit Child Element: Remove the two child limit from April 2026, taking 450,000 children out of poverty
measures.group: Tackling child poverty and reforming welfare
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Universal Credit: Extend the £2,500 surplus earnings threshold for one year from 6 April 2026
measures.group: Tackling child poverty and reforming welfare
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Child Benefit: Exempt 16–19-year-olds with an illness or disability from the 12-hour weekly rule and equalise the treatment of non-standard educational settings from 1 September 2025
measures.group: Tackling child poverty and reforming welfare
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Carer’s Allowance Review: Reassess overpayments from 2015 to 2025 caused by incorrect operational guidance
measures.group: Tackling child poverty and reforming welfare
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Housing Benefit: Reduce the financial cliff edge for claimants in supported housing and temporary accommodation from Autumn 2026
measures.group: Tackling child poverty and reforming welfare
measures.head: spend

measures.name: DWP Fraud and Error: Extend Targeted Case Review of Universal Credit to 2030‑31
measures.group: Tackling child poverty and reforming welfare
measures.head: spend

measures.name: DWP Fraud and Error: Improve accuracy in Pension Credit claims from April 2026
measures.group: Tackling child poverty and reforming welfare
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Health and Disability Benefits: Improve operations by increasing face-to-face assessments, increasing WCA reassessment capability, and PIP award review changes, starting from April 2026
measures.group: Tackling child poverty and reforming welfare
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Motability: Introduce VAT at the standard rate on Advance Payments paid to Motability or equivalent schemes, and Insurance Premium Tax at the standard rate on insurance related to vehicle leases, from 1 July 2026
measures.group: Tackling child poverty and reforming welfare
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Housing Benefit and Pension Credit Administration: Bring together the administration of pensioner Housing Benefit and Pension Credit from Autumn 2026
measures.group: Tackling child poverty and reforming welfare
measures.head: spend

measures.name: National Insurance: Remove access to Class 2 National Insurance contributions (NICs) and increase the initial residency and contributions history requirements for Class 3 NICs for individuals abroad from 6 April 2026
measures.group: Tackling child poverty and reforming welfare
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Rebuilding Britain: Accelerate delivery of growth-enhancing capital investment, including the Lower Thames Crossing
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Business Rates: Introduce both a three year Transitional Relief scheme, partially funded by a 1p Transitional Relief Supplement in 2026/27, and Supporting Small Business schemes from 1 April 2026
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Business Rates: Introduce two new lower multipliers for eligible retail, hospitality and leisure properties funded by a new high-value multiplier from 1 April 2026
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Enterprise Management Incentives (EMI): Increase eligibility to allow scale-ups, as well as start-ups, to access the scheme from 6 April 2026
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Venture Capital Schemes: Increase the Venture Capital Trust (VCT) scheme and the Enterprise Investment Scheme (EIS) annual and lifetime investment limits and the gross assets test from 6 April 2026
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Venture Capital Schemes: Reduce the VCT scheme Income Tax relief from 6 April 2026
measures.head: tax

measures.name: UK Listing Relief: Stamp Duty Reserve Tax relief for transfers of a company's securities for a three-year period from the point of listing, effective from 27 November 2025
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Jobs and Skills: Invest in Youth Guarantee, Growth and Skills Levy, and employment & skills support
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Planning Capacity and Capability: Fund additional capacity in the planning system to get Britain building
measures.head: spend

measures.name: British Business Bank: Expand the Growth Guarantee Scheme to support businesses impacted by changes in global tariffs
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Clamping Down on Illegal High Street Operations: Invest in a new cross-government taskforce, additional Insolvency Service staff and enhanced Trading Standards and law enforcement capabilities
measures.head: spend

measures.name: VAT: Introduce a relief for business donations of goods to charity for onward distribution or use in the delivery of their services, from 1 April 2026
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Cross-border VAT Grouping: Revert to unconditional whole entity cross-border VAT grouping from 26 November 2025
measures.head: tax

measures.name: National Level Regulation: Provide funding to reduce regulatory burden for large food businesses
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Fisheries and Coastal Growth: Launch a fund to support the domestic fishing sector and coastal communities
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Innovation in Wales: Invest in a world-leading semiconductor technologies cluster
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Northern Ireland: Post-Brexit trade support
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Kernow Industrial Growth Fund: Provide funding to support growth in Cornwall
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Business Rates Retention: Extend Greater London Authority enhanced business rates retention arrangements, and pilot Business Rate Retentions for West England Combined Authority, Cornwall, and Liverpool City Region, for three years from April 2026
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Port Talbot: Remediate contaminated brownfield land adjacent to the Celtic Freeport
measures.head: spend

measures.name: RDEL: Go further on efficiencies and savings
measures.group: Cutting waste and investing in public services
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Health and Social Care: Bringing forward SR25 funding to support the abolition of NHS England and unlock savings
measures.group: Cutting waste and investing in public services
measures.head: spend

measures.name: NHS: Investing in NHS technology to improve productivity
measures.group: Cutting waste and investing in public services
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Home Office: Provide additional funding to tackle people smuggling gangs
measures.group: Cutting waste and investing in public services
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Systems & Compliance: Invest in HMRC, DWP and other departments to: reduce fraud and error in the welfare system & public sector; ensure tax compliance and implement Budget tax measures; and increase departmental resilience to economic shocks
measures.group: Cutting waste and investing in public services
measures.head: spend

measures.name: National Year of Reading: Fund state-funded secondary schools in England to increase book supplies
measures.group: Cutting waste and investing in public services
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Investing in Communities: Provide funding to refurbish and improve up to 200 playgrounds in England
measures.group: Cutting waste and investing in public services
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Environmental Regeneration: Launch a new grant scheme for public bodies to support land remediation and reinvest water company fines in projects to clean up rivers, lakes and seas
measures.group: Cutting waste and investing in public services
measures.head: spend

measures.name: UK-EU Deal: Fund DEFRA costs in 2025‑26 for domestic implementation of UK-EU Sanitary and Phytosanitary Agreement
measures.group: Cutting waste and investing in public services
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Personal Tax: Maintain the personal income tax and equivalent national insurance thresholds at current levels for a further three years until April 2031
measures.head: tax

measures.name: National Insurance: Maintain the secondary threshold for employer contributions at current level for a further three years until April 2031
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Student Loans: Freeze Plan 2 repayment threshold for three years from 6 April 2027
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Income: Introduce separate tax rates for property income at 22% for the property basic rate, 42% for the property higher rate and 47% for the property additional rate, from 6 April 2027
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Dividend Income: Increase tax rates on dividend income by 2ppts at the ordinary and upper rate from 6 April 2026
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Savings Income: Increase tax rates on savings income by 2ppts at the basic, higher and additional rate from 6 April 2027 and maintain the Starting Rate of Savings limit at £5000 from April 2026 to April 2031
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Salary Sacrifice: Limit the value of salary sacrificed pension contributions that can receive employee and employer NICs relief to £2,000 per year from 6 April 2029
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Capital Gains Tax: Reduce Capital Gains Tax relief on qualifying disposals to employee ownership trusts from 100% to 50% from 26 November 2025
measures.head: tax

measures.name: High Value Council Tax Surcharge: Introduce a surcharge on owners of residential properties valued over £2 million in England from 1 April 2028
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Inheritance Tax: Maintain the nil-rate band, residence nil-rate band, and allowance for 100% rate of agricultural property relief and business property relief for a further year, from April 2030 until April 2031
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Cap inheritance tax trust charges at £5 million for historic trusts settled by former non‑domiciled individuals from 6 April 2025 and close post‑departure trade profits loophole from 6 April 2026
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Writing-down Allowances: Reduce the main rate writing-down allowance to 14% from April 2026 and introduce a new 40% first-year allowance from 1 January 2026
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Air Passenger Duty: Extend the scope of the higher rate to cover all private jets over 5.7 tonnes from 1 April 2027
measures.head: tax

measures.name: HMRC: Further measures to close the tax gap
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Gambling Duty: Increase Remote Gaming Duty to 40% from 1 April 2026, introduce a new Remote Betting Rate at 25% (excluding Self-Service Betting Terminals, spread betting, pool betting & UK horseracing) from 1 April 2027, and abolish Bingo Duty from 1 April 2026
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Gambling Commission: Provide funding to tackle the illegal market
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Tour Operators’ Margin Scheme: Exclude Private Hire Vehicle Services from the scope of the scheme from 2 January 2026
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Low Value Imports: Reform the customs treatment of low value imports from March 2029
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Emissions Trading Scheme (ETS): Expansion of the UK ETS to International Maritime Routes from 2028
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Defined Benefit (DB) Pension Scheme Surplus Extraction: Introduce flexibilities for employers and direct payments to members from April 2027
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Landfill Tax: Increase the lower rate by the cash increase of the standard rate from 1 April 2026 and in each year of the forecast period
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Soft Drink Industry Levy: Reduce the levy threshold from 5g to 4.5g/100ml and extend to milk-based drinks and milk substitutes from 1 January 2028
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Non-reimbursed Homeworking Expenses: Remove the tax relief available from 6 April 2026
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM): Remove indirect emissions from scope of the CBAM from 1 January 2027
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Advanced Corporation Tax (ACT) reform: Abolish shadow ACT restrictions to relax the limits on companies’ use of surplus ACT balances from 1 April 2026
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Electric Vehicle Excise Duty (eVED): Introduce a new mileage supplement for electric and plug-in hybrid cars from 1 April 2028
measures.group: Modernising motoring tax and supporting the British automative industry
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Support for British automotive industry: Provide additional Electric Car Grant funding & extend to 2029‑30 and invest in EV charging infrastructure
measures.group: Modernising motoring tax and supporting the British automative industry
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Support for British automotive industry: Increase the Expensive Car Supplement threshold for zero emission vehicles to £50,000, from 1 April 2026
measures.group: Modernising motoring tax and supporting the British automative industry
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Support for British automotive industry: Delay bringing Employee Car Ownership schemes within the Benefit in Kind rules from 6 April 2026 to 6 April 2030, with a two year transition period
measures.group: Modernising motoring tax and supporting the British automative industry
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Support for British automotive industry: Extend 100% first-year allowances for zero-emission cars and electric vehicle charge points to 31 March 2027 for Corporation Tax and 5 April 2027 for Income Tax
measures.group: Modernising motoring tax and supporting the British automative industry
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Sizewell C: Reclassify construction costs and recognise income generated through the Regulated Asset Base levy
measures.group: Previously announced policy and other changes
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Plug-in hybrid electric vehicle (PHEV) emissions regulatory standard changes and Benefit in Kind easement
measures.group: Previously announced policy and other changes
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Student Finance: Confirm policy detail for the Lifelong Learning Entitlement launch on 1 January 2027 and increase spending on student loans due to a new means-tested maintenance grant offer for students studying certain courses from academic year 2028/29
measures.group: Previously announced policy and other changes
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Supporting Savers: Make the Help to Save scheme permanent, maintain total ISA annual subscription limit at £20,000 with cash limit reduced to £12,000 for under‑65s from April 2027, delay ISA digitalisation until April 2028 and maintain the ISA subscription limits until 2030/31
measures.group: Previously announced policy and other changes
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Agricultural Property Relief and Business Property Relief: Allow any unused allowance for the 100% rate of relief to be transferable between spouses and civil partners from 6 April 2026
measures.group: Previously announced policy and other changes
measures.head: tax

measures.name: British Coal Staff Superannuation Scheme: Transfer investment reserve to scheme members
measures.group: Previously announced policy and other changes
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Defined Benefit Pensions: Provide inflation protection for pre-1997 pensions in the Pension Protection Fund (PPF) and Financial Assistance Scheme (FAS) where members’ former schemes provided it, from 1 January 2027
measures.group: Previously announced policy and other changes
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Personal Independence Payment: Not proceeding with Spring Statement 2025 reforms to eligibility
measures.group: Previously announced policy and other changes
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Winter Fuel Payment: Target to pensioners with taxable income below or equal to £35,000 from Winter 2025
measures.group: Previously announced policy and other changes
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Universal Credit: Changes to the standard allowance and health element to protect existing claimants and new health element claimants who meet the Severe Conditions Criteria from April 2026
measures.group: Previously announced policy and other changes
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Loan Charge: Government response to the independent review
measures.group: Previously announced policy and other changes
measures.head: tax

measures.name: Compensation Payments: Make compensation available to those affected by Post Office Capture IT software shortfalls and deliver recommendations from Volume 1 of the Post Office Horizon IT Inquiry's final report
measures.group: Previously announced policy and other changes
measures.head: spend

measures.name: Tariffs: Changes since Spring 2025
measures.group: Previously announced policy and other changes
measures.head: tax

footnotes.1: Costings reflect the OBR’s latest economic and fiscal determinants. Totals may not sum due to rounding.
footnotes.2: Measures with no net increase to borrowing are not set out on this presentational scorecard. These are increases to levies (Economic Crime Levy, Financial Conduct Authority levies, Immigration Skills Charge, International Student Levy) to fund spending on government priorities, and reclassification of spend for Mayoral Combined Authorities and police & fire pensions. AME and tax costings with an impact of less than ±£10 million in every year are excluded from the scorecard.
footnotes.3: Many measures have both tax and spend impacts. Measures are identified as tax or spend on the basis of their largest impact.
footnotes.4: Includes additional RDEL investment across the SR25 period of £725m for the Growth and Skills Levy and £425m for the Youth Guarantee. This is supported by funding previously allocated at SR25, which will help deliver an £820m Youth Guarantee across the SR25 period.
footnotes.5: Full costings for the measures in this package are set out in the Budget 2025 Published Costings Document available on gov.uk
